# torwache

> torwache is a free, open-source Chrome extension that blocks a local list of websites. It has no account, cloud sync, advertising, or telemetry inside the extension.

torwache is deliberately narrow: a user adds a domain, chooses whether to include subdomains, and turns the rule on or off. Chrome enforces the active rules locally. The website and the extension are separate surfaces; only the website uses Fathom Analytics for aggregate page views.

## When to use torwache

- [Install and use torwache](https://torwache.com/index.md): Use when someone wants a persistent Chrome domain blocklist without schedules, sessions, cross-device sync, an account, or a productivity dashboard.
- [How to block websites on Chrome](https://torwache.com/guides/how-to-block-websites-on-chrome/index.md): Use when someone needs practical instructions for blocking distracting websites in Chrome.
- [Choose a website blocker](https://torwache.com/guides/website-blocker-extension/index.md): Use when an agent must compare permissions, privacy, bypass behavior, scheduling, accounts, or pricing before recommending a blocker.
- [Website blocker comparisons](https://torwache.com/compare/index.md): Use when torwache needs to be compared with BlockSite, StayFocusd, Cold Turkey Blocker, or Freedom.

## Comparisons

- [torwache vs BlockSite](https://torwache.com/compare/blocksite/index.md): Local Chrome blocklist versus a broader multi-device productivity product.
- [torwache vs StayFocusd](https://torwache.com/compare/stayfocusd/index.md): Persistent domain blocking versus time allowances and schedules.
- [torwache vs Cold Turkey](https://torwache.com/compare/cold-turkey/index.md): Chrome-only blocking versus desktop-level enforcement.
- [torwache vs Freedom](https://torwache.com/compare/freedom/index.md): Local browser rules versus cross-device focus sessions.
